From e5e890630533bdc15b26a34bb8e7ef539bdf1322 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Fernando Fernandez Mancera <fmancera@suse.de>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 13:03:56 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] net: bridge: fix nd_tbl NULL dereference when IPv6 is
 disabled

When booting with the 'ipv6.disable=1' parameter, the nd_tbl is never
initialized because inet6_init() exits before ndisc_init() is called
which initializes it. Then, if neigh_suppress is enabled and an ICMPv6
Neighbor Discovery packet reaches the bridge, br_do_suppress_nd() will
dereference ipv6_stub->nd_tbl which is NULL, passing it to
neigh_lookup(). This causes a kernel NULL pointer dereference.

 BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000268
 Oops: 0000 [#1] PREEMPT SMP NOPTI
 [...]
 RIP: 0010:neigh_lookup+0x16/0xe0
 [...]
 Call Trace:
  <IRQ>
  ? neigh_lookup+0x16/0xe0
  br_do_suppress_nd+0x160/0x290 [bridge]
  br_handle_frame_finish+0x500/0x620 [bridge]
  br_handle_frame+0x353/0x440 [bridge]
  __netif_receive_skb_core.constprop.0+0x298/0x1110
  __netif_receive_skb_one_core+0x3d/0xa0
  process_backlog+0xa0/0x140
  __napi_poll+0x2c/0x170
  net_rx_action+0x2c4/0x3a0
  handle_softirqs+0xd0/0x270
  do_softirq+0x3f/0x60

Fix this by replacing IS_ENABLED(IPV6) call with ipv6_mod_enabled() in
the callers. This is in essence disabling NS/NA suppression when IPv6 is
disabled.

Fixes: ed842faeb2bd ("bridge: suppress nd pkts on BR_NEIGH_SUPPRESS ports")
Reported-by: Guruprasad C P <gurucp2005@gmail.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/netdev/CAHXs0ORzd62QOG-Fttqa2Cx_A_VFp=utE2H2VTX5nqfgs7LDxQ@mail.gmail.com/
Signed-off-by: Fernando Fernandez Mancera <fmancera@suse.de>
Reviewed-by: Ido Schimmel <idosch@nvidia.com>
Acked-by: Nikolay Aleksandrov <razor@blackwall.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260304120357.9778-1-fmancera@suse.de
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/bridge/br_device.c b/net/bridge/br_device.c
index ee01122f466f..f7502e62dd35 100644
--- a/net/bridge/br_device.c
+++ b/net/bridge/br_device.c
@@ -74,7 +74,7 @@ netdev_tx_t br_dev_xmit(struct sk_buff *skb, struct net_device *dev)
 	     eth_hdr(skb)->h_proto == htons(ETH_P_RARP)) &&
 	    br_opt_get(br, BROPT_NEIGH_SUPPRESS_ENABLED)) {
 		br_do_proxy_suppress_arp(skb, br, vid, NULL);
-	} else if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6) &&
+	} else if (ipv6_mod_enabled() &&
 		   skb->protocol == htons(ETH_P_IPV6) &&
 		   br_opt_get(br, BROPT_NEIGH_SUPPRESS_ENABLED) &&
 		   pskb_may_pull(skb, sizeof(struct ipv6hdr) +

diff --git a/net/bridge/br_input.c b/net/bridge/br_input.c
index 1405f1061a54..2cbae0f9ae1f 100644
--- a/net/bridge/br_input.c
+++ b/net/bridge/br_input.c
@@ -170,7 +170,7 @@ int br_handle_frame_finish(struct net *net, struct sock *sk, struct sk_buff *skb
 	    (skb->protocol == htons(ETH_P_ARP) ||
 	     skb->protocol == htons(ETH_P_RARP))) {
 		br_do_proxy_suppress_arp(skb, br, vid, p);
-	} else if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6) &&
+	} else if (ipv6_mod_enabled() &&
 		   skb->protocol == htons(ETH_P_IPV6) &&
 		   br_opt_get(br, BROPT_NEIGH_SUPPRESS_ENABLED) &&
 		   pskb_may_pull(skb, sizeof(struct ipv6hdr) +
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a kernel NULL pointer dereference in the bridge module that occurs when IPv6 is disabled at boot (`ipv6.disable=1`) and neighbor suppression is enabled. The root cause is that `nd_tbl` is never initialized under this condition, but the code used `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` (a compile-time check) to guard calls into IPv6 neighbor functions. This check passes even when IPv6 is disabled at runtime, leading to a dereference of a NULL `nd_tbl`.

### Changes per file

1. **net/bridge/br_device.c** (line 77)  
   Changed the condition from `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` to `ipv6_mod_enabled()` before the call to `br_do_proxy_suppress_arp()` for IPv6 packets. This ensures the suppression logic is only invoked when the IPv6 module is actually enabled at runtime.

2. **net/bridge/br_input.c** (line 173)  
   Made the identical change: replaced `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` with `ipv6_mod_enabled()` in the condition that guards `br_do_proxy_suppress_arp()` for incoming IPv6 neighbor discovery packets.

### Relationship between the modifications

Both changes address the same bug and follow the same pattern. They convert a compile-time check into a runtime check that accurately reflects whether IPv6 is active. The two locations represent the two code paths where the bridge processes IPv6 packets for neighbor suppression (egress in `br_dev_xmit` and ingress in `br_handle_frame_finish`). By applying the fix in both places, the patch ensures that bridge neighbor suppression is completely disabled when IPv6 is not available at runtime, regardless of the packet direction.

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### Modifications in Each File

1. **net/bridge/br_input.c**  
   - **Change:** In `br_handle_frame_finish()`, replaced the compile-time check `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` with the runtime check `ipv6_mod_enabled()` for the condition that handles ICMPv6 Neighbor Discovery packet suppression (`br_do_suppress_nd`).  
   - **Effect:** This ensures that when IPv6 is disabled at boot (via `ipv6.disable=1`), the code does not attempt to use the uninitialized `nd_tbl`, preventing a NULL pointer dereference.

2. **net/bridge/br_device.c**  
   - **Change:** In `br_dev_xmit()`, the same substitution: `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` → `ipv6_mod_enabled()` for the corresponding suppression path on locally generated IPv6 traffic.  
   - **Effect:** Same as above; avoids referencing the NULL `nd_tbl` when IPv6 is disabled.

### Relationship Between Modifications

Both changes fix the identical root cause: the original code used a compile-time check (`IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)`) which evaluates to `true` as long as the kernel is built with IPv6 support, even if IPv6 is disabled at runtime via kernel parameter. When IPv6 is disabled, `nd_tbl` (the neighbour table for IPv6) remains uninitialized, leading to a NULL pointer dereference when `neigh_lookup()` is called. By replacing with `ipv6_mod_enabled()`—a runtime check that returns `false` when IPv6 is disabled—the bridge gracefully skips the suppression logic before any dereference occurs. The two modifications are symmetric and protect both the input (received frames) and output (locally sent frames) paths that invoke ND suppression.

2.34.1

The patch fixes a NULL pointer dereference in the bridge's neighbor suppression (NS/NA) code when IPv6 is disabled at boot via `ipv6.disable=1`. The issue occurs because the `nd_tbl` is never initialized when IPv6 is disabled, but `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` still evaluates true at compile time, allowing the code to call `neigh_lookup()` with a NULL pointer.

**Modifications in each file:**

1. **net/bridge/br_device.c** (line 77):  
   Changed `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` to `ipv6_mod_enabled()` in the condition that triggers `br_do_proxy_suppress_arp` (which internally handles ND suppression). This ensures the suppression code is only executed when IPv6 is actually enabled at runtime.

2. **net/bridge/br_input.c** (line 173):  
   Similarly replaced `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` with `ipv6_mod_enabled()` in the condition that invokes ND suppression during frame handling.

**Relationship between changes:**  
Both modifications target the same root cause—use of a compile-time check (`IS_ENABLED`) that cannot account for runtime IPv6 disablement. By switching to a runtime check (`ipv6_mod_enabled()`), both callers now correctly skip the ND suppression logic when IPv6 is disabled, preventing the dereference of the uninitialized `nd_tbl`. The two changes are independent but address the same bug in different code paths (transmit and receive sides of the bridge).

           ...

This avoids the NULL dereference of `nd_tbl` in `neigh_lookup()`.
